title: Subscription credential support in the launcher
description: Human requirement (REPL, 2026-08-19): the fleet must run on a Claude SUBSCRIPTION, not only an API key. MEASURED: Claude Code mints a long-lived subscription OAuth token via `claude setup-token`, honored through the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var (the canary worker's live probe roster lists it beside ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN); the wrapper's spawn env allowlist ALREADY forwards the CLAUDE_* prefix to children (agent-spawn-environment.ts:22), so no spawn-side change exists. THE ONLY GAP: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.ts refuses the launch when the agent command is claude and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent (the refusal block near :114-119), even when CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is present — a false refusal for subscription users. Deliverable: widen the credential predicate to any-of-three (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN); the refusal message names ALL THREE accepted variables plus the `claude setup-token` subscription path; the provenance disclosure reports WHICH credential kind satisfied it (name only, never the value). Update docs/agent-stack-runbook.md's env table and the shipped artifact's INSTALL.md text (source lives with the pack tooling from task-3ac5c237) to document the subscription path as primary for individual users. NOT in scope: Codex subscription auth (Codex adapter is parked v0.2 — recorded separately in M4), any change to agent-spawn-environment.ts (allowlist already correct), keychain reading (bare mode skips it by design). Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; test (count line); pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The launcher accepts any one of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN as satisfying the claude-command credential requirement; each accepted-alone case is a test arm, and the all-absent refusal names all three variables plus the setup-token hint, asserted exactly.

Provenance reports which credential VARIABLE satisfied the requirement by name; no test or log path ever prints a credential value, asserted by a sweep over the launcher's output on a fixture credential.
Runbook env table and the artifact INSTALL text document the subscription path (claude setup-token -> CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) as the individual-user default, API key as the alternative.

WHAT EACH ARM PINS, in the plan's letters:
(a) ACCEPTED-ALONE x3, generated from one roster so a name cannot be silently dropped from the loop: each resolves ok:true, the satisfying entry is source PRESET + secret true, and the disclosure line reads `<NAME>=<preset, hidden>`.
(b) THE DELIVERY MAP, the load-bearing arm: with ONLY CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set, `config.env["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"]` must equal the fixture token — i.e. the overlay that moe-up-main merges into childEnv carries the name claude 2.1.235 actually honors — and that entry must be source MINTED, secret, rendered `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<minted, hidden>` with the value absent from the lines.
(c) NO-OVERWRITE: with both the alias and a DIFFERENT operator-supplied ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, the launcher contributes NOTHING under that name — `config.env["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"]` is undefined and no variables entry exists. Absence is the assertion because the overlay WINS over the parent env at moe-up-main.ts:185; anything the launcher puts there shadows the operator's own token.
(d) ALL-ABSENT refusal: exactly one refusal, code MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING (stable, unchanged), `variable` = the joined roster, and the message asserted as a hand-written exact string — `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (set one; run `claude setup-token` for a subscription token)`. Hand-written rather than rebuilt from the roster: rebuilding it from production's own constant would assert nothing about the three names an operator actually needs to read.
(e) NON-CLAUDE waiver regression kept, renamed to say "no credential at all"; the absolute-path/.cmd/CLAUDE.EXE arm now expects the joined-roster variable.
(f) PROVENANCE + PRECEDENCE: with all three present the reported satisfier is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and the other two are absent from `variables`. The test name says PRESENCE ORDER AT THE GATE explicitly — it is not a claim about how claude resolves auth internally, and I do not want a future reader to mistake it for one.
(g) VALUE-NEVER-PRINTED SWEEP over a NONZERO line count: `expect(lines.length).toBeGreaterThan(8)` BEFORE the value search, so a sweep that silently collected zero lines cannot pass; the swept corpus includes the mapped/minted entry's disclosure and the refusal message, and all three fixture values must appear nowhere.

moe-up-env.ts 169 -> 230 lines (+61, cap 250 respected; the budget was ~+20 and the overrun is documentation — the measured-probe rationale lives in the code where the next reader meets the mapping, not only in a task comment that will not travel with the file).

(1) ROSTER + REFUSAL. `CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_VARIABLES = Object.freeze(["CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN","ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN","ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] as const)`, documented subscription-first. `refuse()` became `refuseCredential()`: the stable published code MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING is UNCHANGED, `variable` now carries the joined roster, and the message is `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (set one; run `claude setup-token` for a subscription token)`. Consumers re-grepped before changing it: the only matches on MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING outside the module are moe-up-main.test.ts:126, docs/agent-stack-runbook.md:28 and tools/packaging/pack-docs.ts:38 — the first is re-pinned below, the other two are step 4. No production consumer matches on the message SHAPE, only on the code, which is why widening the message is safe.

(2) PROVENANCE. The satisfying variable is surfaced as a secret PRESET entry in `variables`, so the existing `describeLaunchVariables` path renders it `<preset, hidden>` — zero new printing code, the sworn secret path is reused rather than duplicated.

(3) THE DELIVERY MAP, the load-bearing half. `claudeCredentials()` walks the roster in order and, when the satisfier is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN **and** ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is absent, appends a second MINTED secret entry `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` carrying the same value. That entry rides the pre-existing overlay loop into `resolution.env`, which moe-up-main.ts:185 merges into `childEnv` and hands to both children — so a subscription user's token reaches `claude --bare` under the only name it honors at 2.1.235. Both clauses of that condition are LIVE and separately covered: drop the name clause and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY-alone would be re-exported as an auth token (caught by the exact overlay key-set arm); drop the absence clause and an operator's own ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN would be shadowed by the alias value (caught by the no-overwrite arm). Neither is a dead guard.

(4) COMMENT. The predicate comment now states: bare mode reads no keychain; any of the three satisfies acceptance; CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is an ALIAS accepted for convenience and delivered as ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN because `claude -p --bare` ignores the alias name — with the measurement dated (2026-08-19, claude 2.1.235, three arms over one token value plus a no-credential control) and an explicit instruction to re-probe when the CLI version moves. The version-dated caveat lives in the code, next to the thing that goes stale.

`isClaudeCommand` and the non-claude waiver are byte-identical; the waiver path now yields an empty credential array rather than skipping a refusal, which is the same observable behaviour and is pinned by the untouched "needs no credential at all once MOE_AGENT_COMMAND names a non-claude command" arm.

STEP-1 EVIDENCE — worker-a211f4b4, at HEAD a675772b (identical to plan HEAD). The governor-mandated live probe FAILED for CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, independently reproducing architect-6c720ab6's comment-0e000104. Full record here; the block reason is the short form.

(1) REFUSAL SITE CONFIRMED UNCHANGED. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.ts is 169 lines; the predicate at :116-118 reads exactly

sole accepted variable ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; `refuse()` (:93-98) builds `{code: MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING, message: `${MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING}: ${variableName}`, variable}`; `describeLaunchVariables` (:151-169) renders secret entries `<${SOURCE_WORD[source]}, hidden>` and never a value. Read-only confirm of agent-spawn-environment.ts: PROVIDER_ENVIRONMENT_PREFIXES (:21-23) is `["ANTHROPIC_", "AWS_", "AZURE_", "CLAUDE_", "GOOGLE_", "VERTEX_"]` — both prefixes forwarded, NOT edited (task rail 1).

(2) LIVE PROBE — THREE ARMS, ONE TOKEN VALUE, DISCRIMINATING. claude 2.1.235 (same build the architect probed). Child env scrubbed of all four of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, then ONE variable set per arm. Command identical in every arm: `claude -p --bare "say OK"`. Token value never echoed — the harness redacts it out of both streams before printing, and no arm printed the variable.
  C  negative control, NO credential      -> exit 1, "Not logged in · Please run /login"   (2791 ms)
  A  CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<token>      -> exit 1, "Not logged in · Please run /login"   (2505 ms)
  B  ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<same token>    -> exit 0, "Hi! What can I help you with?"       (5858 ms)
Arm A is byte-identical to the no-credential control: supplying the credential under that name changes NOTHING. Arm B proves the token itself is valid and the binary authenticates — so A's failure is the variable NAME, not a bad token, not a broken install, not an expired session.

Credential provenance: the host's existing subscription OAuth credential (claudeAiOauth.accessToken, scopes include user:inference, expiresAt 2026-08-19T18:38:41Z — 185 min of validity remaining at probe time). I did NOT run `claude setup-token`: minting a new long-lived account credential is not a step I will take unasked, and it is unnecessary here because the architect already probed a setup-token value and got the SAME split. Two different token KINDS, same version, same outcome — that is stronger evidence than either probe alone.

(3) WHAT THIS FALSIFIES. The task description's central measured claim — "Claude Code mints a long-lived subscription OAuth token via `claude setup-token`, honored through the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var" — is FALSE for `--bare` at 2.1.235. The description infers it from the canary's probe ROSTER, but a roster of variables a probe checks is not evidence any of them authenticates.

(4) THE DELIVERY PATH IS MEASURED AND THE FIX IS IN-SCOPE. moe-up-main.ts:185 `const childEnv = { ...options.env, ...resolution.env };` and that childEnv is handed to both the daemon child and the wrapper spawn (:213-214). So an overlay entry minted inside moe-up-env.ts REACHES claude children, and a name-mapping fix needs NO change to agent-spawn-environment.ts and stays entirely inside this task's owned paths.

(5) WHY I AM BLOCKING RATHER THAN BUILDING. Step 1 instructs report_blocked on probe failure and "do NOT widen the gate to a credential that cannot authenticate", and the governor made that a hard gate. Independently, two DoD items are unsatisfiable as written without violating epic rail 3 (honest surface — claims match measured behavior): DoD 1 accepts CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN as satisfying the requirement, and DoD 3 documents `claude setup-token -> CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` as the individual-user DEFAULT. Both would ship a path I have measured does not authenticate. Plan step 3 as written is pure acceptance-widening with no delivery mapping — precisely the "naive pass-through" the architect warned of. It would convert today's honest false REFUSAL into a false ACCEPTANCE that fails later, inside the wrapper's children, looking exactly like the orchestration bug moe-up-env.ts's own header comment says it exists to prevent. That is a worse product than the current bug.

(6) SUGGESTED REPLAN, offered as input not authority — one added step, the rest of the plan survives:
  (a) Roster and acceptance: keep any-of-three.
  (b) DELIVERY MAP: when the satisfying variable is CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is absent but ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN present), emit `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` into the resolution overlay carrying that value, so children receive the name the binary honors. Test arm: resolution.env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is set when only CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN was supplied. This is the load-bearing detail.
  (c) DOCS: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN is the canonical subscription variable at 2.1.235; `claude setup-token` mints the VALUE, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is accepted as an alias the launcher maps. Do not document the alias as the working default.
  (d) Pin the probe as a durable arm or a documented version-dated limitation — the architect is right that CLI auth behavior moves between versions, and (b) silently becomes wrong the day CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN starts working.
Alternative if the mapping is judged out of scope: narrow this task to acceptance + honest docs naming ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN as the subscription variable, and file the mapping as its own row. I have no preference; both are honest. What I will not do is ship (a) alone.

NOT MEASURED, stated so nobody assumes it: I did not test whether CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN works for NON-bare `claude -p` (irrelevant here — the wrapper uses --bare), did not test Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry paths, and did not run the baseline gates, since no code change is being proposed under this plan.
